User.title: User
User.description: Represents a client user registered in the BidFlow Connect application. Stores essential profile information, payment status, and a reference to their active onboarding submission.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The email address of the user.

fullName.description: The full name of the user.

businessName.description: The registered business name of the client.

role.description: The role of the user within the system (e.g., 'client', 'admin').

subscriptionStatus.description: The current payment or subscription status of the user (e.g., 'active', 'inactive', 'cancelled', 'past_due').

stripeCustomerId.description: The customer ID generated by Stripe for this user. Null if not yet associated with a Stripe customer.

stripeSubscriptionId.description: The ID of the active subscription associated with this user in Stripe. Null if no active subscription.

onboardingStatus.description: The current status of the user's onboarding process (e.g., 'not_started', 'in_progress', 'ready_for_review', 'submitted').

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user profile was last updated.

onboardingSubmissionId.description: Reference to the unique identifier of the user's current or latest OnboardingSubmission. (Relationship: User 1:1 OnboardingSubmission). Null if onboarding has not started or no active submission.

OnboardingSubmission.title: OnboardingSubmission
OnboardingSubmission.description: Represents a single instance of a client's onboarding process, storing all responses, progress, and submission status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the OnboardingSubmission entity.

userId.description: Reference to the unique identifier of the User who owns this onboarding submission. (Relationship: User 1:N OnboardingSubmission)

businessName.description: The business name of the client submitting the onboarding, denormalized from User for convenience.

status.description: The current overall status of the onboarding submission (e.g., 'not_started', 'in_progress', 'ready_for_review', 'submitted').

currentStep.description: The key of the last completed or currently active step in the onboarding wizard, guiding the user where to continue.

completedSteps.description: An array of keys representing the steps that have been successfully completed in the onboarding process.

completionPercentage.description: The calculated percentage of the onboarding process that has been completed (0-100).

selectedServices.description: An array of strings representing the services the client selected for support in Step 4, which determines conditional modules.

enabledModules.description: An object indicating which conditional onboarding modules are enabled based on selected services.

sections.description: An object containing the responses for each onboarding section, keyed by section identifier. Each value is an object holding specific form field data for that section.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the onboarding submission was initially created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the onboarding submission was last updated by any action.

lastSavedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the onboarding submission was last explicitly saved or autosaved, for user feedback.

submittedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the onboarding submission was finally completed and submitted. Null until submitted.

adminReopened.description: True if an administrator has reopened a submitted onboarding pack for further client edits.

googleDriveFolderId.description: The ID of the dedicated Google Drive folder created for this submission's exported data and documents. Null until exported.

googleDriveFolderUrl.description: The URL of the dedicated Google Drive folder created for this submission's exported data and documents. Null until exported.

UploadedDocument.title: UploadedDocument
UploadedDocument.description: Stores metadata for a document uploaded by a client during the onboarding process, linked to a specific submission.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UploadedDocument entity.

userId.description: Reference to the unique identifier of the User who uploaded this document. (Relationship: User 1:N UploadedDocument)

onboardingSubmissionId.description: Reference to the unique identifier of the OnboardingSubmission this document belongs to. (Relationship: OnboardingSubmission 1:N UploadedDocument)

sectionKey.description: The key of the onboarding section where this document was relevantly uploaded or associated (e.g., 'complianceInsurance').

category.description: The category of the uploaded document (e.g., 'Insurance Certificate', 'Capability Statement').

fileName.description: The original name of the file when it was uploaded by the user.

contentType.description: The MIME type of the uploaded file (e.g., 'application/pdf', 'image/jpeg').

size.description: The size of the file in bytes.

storagePath.description: The full path to the file in Firebase Storage, where it is securely stored.

uploadedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the document was uploaded.

driveFileId.description: The ID of the file in Google Drive after it has been successfully exported. Null until exported.

driveFolderId.description: The ID of the Google Drive folder where this file is located after export. Null until exported.

definition.description: Stores client user profiles. The document ID matches the Firebase Auth UID. Includes subscription status, onboarding status, and role for direct authorization checks, ensuring authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The Firebase Authentication UID of the user, serving as the document ID.

definition.description: Stores all client onboarding drafts and final submissions. Includes denormalized 'userId' for authorization independence and 'businessName' for display. This enables efficient queries and simplified security rules by keeping ownership context within the document itself.

params.name: submissionId
params.description: The unique identifier for an onboarding submission.

definition.description: Stores metadata for client-uploaded documents. Includes denormalized 'userId' and 'onboardingSubmissionId' for authorization independence and contextual linking to the user and their specific submission. This supports secure and efficient listing and access control.

params.name: documentId
params.description: The unique identifier for an uploaded document.

definition.description: A collection used for Database-Backed Access Control. The existence of a document in this collection, where 'adminId' matches a user's UID, grants administrative privileges. No additional fields are typically required, as existence is the authorization signal.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed following the core principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Backed Access Control), QAPs (Query-Agnostic Permissions), and Invariants. The primary goal is to ensure robust, scalable, and easily debuggable security rules, particularly by minimizing or eliminating the need for `get()` operations within rules.

1.  **Users (`/users/{userId}`)**: This top-level collection stores client user profiles. Each document ID (`{userId}`) directly corresponds to the Firebase Authentication UID, establishing clear path-based ownership. This ensures that a client can only read and write their own profile (`request.auth.uid == userId`). The `subscriptionStatus` and `onboardingStatus` fields are directly on the user document, enabling quick and independent authorization checks without needing to query other documents. This achieves **Authorization Independence** for user-specific data.

2.  **Onboarding Submissions (`/onboardingSubmissions/{submissionId}`)**: This top-level collection stores all client onboarding drafts and submitted data. Each `onboardingSubmission` document includes a `userId` field. This `userId` is a denormalized authorization context, directly linking the submission to its owner. By placing `onboardingSubmissions` at the top level and including `userId`, we achieve **Authorization Independence** as security rules can directly check `resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid` without `get()` calls to a parent `user` document. This structure also supports **QAPs** by enabling efficient `list` queries for both clients (e.g., `where('userId', '==', request.auth.uid)`) and administrators (listing all submissions), without relying on rules to filter results.

3.  **Uploaded Documents (`/uploadedDocuments/{documentId}`)**: Similar to `onboardingSubmissions`, this top-level collection stores metadata for all client-uploaded documents. Each `uploadedDocument` includes `userId` and `onboardingSubmissionId` fields. These are denormalized values, providing the complete authorization context within each document. This again ensures **Authorization Independence**, as rules can verify ownership (`resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid`) and association with a specific submission without expensive `get()` calls. This also supports **QAPs**, allowing efficient `list` queries for documents belonging to a specific user or submission for both clients and administrators.

4.  **Admins (`/admins/{adminId}`)**: This collection implements DBAC for global roles. An admin user is identified by the mere *existence* of a document in this collection where the document ID (`{adminId}`) matches their Firebase UID. This provides a simple, explicit, and performant way to check for administrative privileges (`exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/admins/$(request.auth.uid))`) without relying on custom claims or complex document content, adhering to the 'Existence over Content' mandate for global roles.

Overall, this design prioritizes flattened, top-level collections with denormalized ownership identifiers (`userId`, `onboardingSubmissionId`) in the documents themselves. This dramatically simplifies security rules by making authorization checks atomic and efficient, preventing `get()` dependency issues, and enabling robust QAPs for all common access patterns for both clients and administrators. The `businessName` is also denormalized where relevant for display convenience, maintaining data clarity.
